summary: bible/characters/index.json records gender 'unspecified' for CHAR-old-crab and CHAR-young-crab, but the source states both are female.

findings.issue: Both entries have gender 'unspecified' with inferred_fields ['gender'] and reason 'No gender stated in the source beyond old/young'. The source does state it: ch003-p43 “an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter … ‘Hold your tongue, Ma!’ said the young Crab”. Mother and daughter are both female.

source.quote: an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter

findings.suggested_fix: Set gender 'female' for both, remove 'gender' from inferred_fields and cite ch003-p43.

findings.issue: Not a conflict, alignment only: these have gender 'unspecified' in the index, but the appearance cards must fix gender to male/female (SOUL gender hard anchor). The cards set Duck male, Lory female, Eaglet female, Canary female, Magpie male, each tagged inferred with reasons.
findings.suggested_fix: character-manager may mirror these inferred values into index.json so voiceprint/casting read one value.

impact: The appearance cards already use the source-backed value (female) for both Crabs; downstream readers of index.json alone would see 'unspecified'.
requested_action: memory-bible routes a controlled change to character-manager; appearance did not edit index.json (outside its write scope).
ruling: (a) Source-stated: both Crabs are female (ch003-p43 'an old Crab ... to her daughter'). The current 'unspecified / no gender stated' is wrong. (b) Alignment only: mirror the appearance cards' inferred values into the index.

(b) Set CHAR-duck male, CHAR-lory female, CHAR-eaglet female, CHAR-canary female, CHAR-magpie male. Keep 'gender' in inferred_fields and copy each reason from the matching appearance.json.
